slides.title:
Design
systems
in 2026
slides.byline: Presented by Lena Brandt, Head of Design
slides.notes: Welcome. Twenty minutes, then questions. The short version: we ship more with fewer parts.

slides.label: What changed
slides.title: We stopped drawing screens and started shipping *rules*.

items.heading: One token set
items.text: Colour, type and spacing live in one file every product reads from.

items.heading: Agents build pages
items.text: Marketing pages are assembled by agents and reviewed by one designer.

items.heading: Fewer components
items.text: We cut the library from 214 to 61 components without losing a layout.

slides.notes: Each of these took about a quarter. The order mattered: tokens first.

slides.label: Delivery speed
slides.title: +184% since we moved to *tokens*
slides.text: The jump came after agents started working from the shared token file instead of screenshots.

slides.title: What we'd do *differently*
slides.text: Three things that cost us a quarter each, and how to skip them.

slides.label: Lessons
slides.title: Do these before you touch a component.
items: Name tokens by role, not by colour
Write the rules down where agents can read them
Give one person the final say on type
Measure what ships, not what's drawn

slides.label: From the teams
slides.quote: The first week felt slower. By week three we had stopped arguing about *spacing* altogether.

slides.label: Where it's going
slides.text: components left in the library, down from 214. Our goal for 2027 is *under 50*.
